The design choices were motivated by the limitations of other graphics APIs: OpenGL is too abstract to exploit modern hardware performance, and OpenCL/compute shaders may not be well-supported on mobile devices or lack correspondence to Vulkan’s subpasses [S1].

The claim is fully supported by the text in Source [S1]. The passage explicitly states: 'OpenGL was another candidate for the graphics pipeline, but it is too abstract to exploit the performance of modern hardware. OpenCL and compute shaders may not be supported well on mobile devices, and they cannot use hardware rasterizers. Moreover, their performances are limited since there is no correspondence to Vulkan’s subpasses.' This matches every part of the claim.

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'OpenGL was another candidate for the graphics pipeline, but it is too abstract to exploit the performance of modern hardware... It solves the problem of integrating reverse-mode AD into a graphics pipeline by using 2D images as primitive data structures instead of multi-dimensional tensors, maintaining compatibility with hardware rasterizers [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that Dressi-AD is a 'hardware-agnostic automatic differentiation library for differentiable rendering built on Vulkan' and that it uses '2D images as the primitives of our AD, considering compatibility with graphics pipeline and DR.' It further clarifies that variables are converted into VkImage structures (2D images) to handle data, and that this approach is chosen specifically to maintain compatibility with the graphics pipeline (avoiding compute shaders which cannot use hardware rasterizers). The claim accurately reflects these points.
supported

They are converted into `VkImage` structures [S1]. `VkImage` handles 2D arrays and can store textures, vertex buffers, blend weight matrices, or higher-dimensional tensors represented as stacked 2D arrays [S1].

The claim states that variables are converted into `VkImage` structures, which handle 2D arrays and can store textures, vertex buffers, blend weight matrices, or higher-dimensional tensors represented as stacked 2D arrays. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'In our implementation, we convert the variables into VkImage. They can contain any 2D array resources, such as textures, vertex buffers, and blend weight matrices. Note that the variables can represent higher dimensional tensors as stacked 2D arrays.' This matches the claim exactly.
supported
# For texture sampling, returns InverseUV backward function [S1]

The claim states that for texture sampling, the system returns an 'InverseUV backward function'. Source [S1] explicitly lists 'I2: Inverse UV in Section 3.3.2' and describes it as 'Regarding the backward computation of texture sampling... we propose an inverse UV texture.' Furthermore, Section 3.3.1 mentions that 'backward functions of texture sampling' are an exception to built-in GLSL functions, and Section 3.3.2 is titled 'Inverse UV: Backward for Hardware Texture Sampler'. Thus, the evidence directly supports the claim.
supported

Dressi-AD instantiates forward function objects and variable objects [S1].

The claim is directly supported by the text in Source [S1]. Specifically, Section 3.3.1 states: 'Dressi-AD instantiates function objects and variable objects in programs written by users.' The notes also confirm that 'Dressi-AD instantiates forward function objects and variable objects' and that 'Variables (inputs and outputs) are converted into VkImage structures' (which are the variable objects).
supported
Standard hardware texture samplers (`texture()`) do not support automatic differentiation, necessitating the Inverse UV backward function [S1].

The evidence explicitly states in Section 3.3.2 that 'Some function objects for DR cannot be defined using the built-in GLSL functions. One such exception is the backward functions of texture sampling,' and subsequently introduces 'Inverse UV' as the solution for the 'backward computation of texture sampling with hardware.' This confirms that standard hardware texture samplers do not support automatic differentiation natively, necessitating the custom Inverse UV backward function.
